solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bachelor tucking into cooked trout — or flatfish

indicators.note: to tuck into something is to go inside it, so one piece sits within the other
cooked figuratively means doctored or altered, so the letters of the fish word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, before rearranging
B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor

explanation.surface: A cook deciding between serving trout or another fish, with a bachelor tucking in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' sounds like eating, which suits the kitchen picture, but it places the bachelor inside the rearranged fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbot is a large European sea fish with both eyes on one side of its body, a classic flat species.

clue.text: Little person going around with nervous tic

indicators.note: going around something means encircling it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: titch is informal British slang for a very small person
W is the common abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A small person moving about while suffering from a nervous tic.
explanation.walkthrough: Titch is British slang for a small person, from the music-hall comedian Little Tich.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden involuntary jerk of a muscle is exactly what a tic is, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Colourful display of East End artist

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a recognised artist
someone located in the East End might be in Bow, a district of East London

explanation.surface: A vivid show staged by a painter from London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: An artist in the East End is an RA in Bow; Bow is a district of East London, traditionally Cockney territory.
explanation.definitionFit: The arc of spectral colours seen in the sky after rain is a striking natural show of many hues.

clue.text: It's a malediction: you can swear it!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a curse or profanity
second meaning: a solemn promise, which is something people swear

explanation.walkthrough: Swear works both ways here: one swears a solemn promise, and a swear word is itself a curse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a profane curse and a formal sworn promise, as in taking one in court.

clue.text: Standing sculptures Moore finally turned out

indicators.note: something turned out is expelled, so that letter is removed from the artworks

parts.note: statues are carved or cast sculptures

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the sculptor's name

parts.note: the last letter of the sculptor Henry Moore's surname

explanation.surface: Henry Moore's statues were eventually ejected from where they stood.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E from STATUES. Henry Moore was a famous British sculptor, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: One's standing in society is one's rank or position, the same idea as social position or prestige.

clue.text: Surprisingly he paints one treading the boards

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is an unexpected one, so these letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor surprises everyone by turning out to be a painter too.
explanation.definitionFit: The boards is an idiom for the theatre stage, so someone walking on it is an actor.

clue.text: Sailor originally keeping an otter

parts.note: tar is an old slang term for a sailor

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of keeping
an is the indefinite article, here as A

explanation.surface: A sailor who started out keeping an otter as a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping' looks like it means containing, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarka the Otter is Henry Williamson's 1927 novel, whose hero is a river animal of that species living in Devon.

clue.text: Butcherbird makes us scream, turning tail

indicators.note: the tail is the end of the word, and turning it means its final pair of letters swap round

parts.note: a shriek is a loud piercing scream

explanation.surface: A butcherbird's behaviour is so alarming that it makes people scream and flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning tail' looks like running away; here it means the last two letters of SHRIEK are swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Butcherbird is a folk name for this songbird, which impales its prey on thorns like a butcher's hooks.

clue.text: Single woman in charge of keeping books? That's ridiculous

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the woman and in-charge pieces hold the books

parts.note: IC is the abbreviation for in charge
Di is a short woman's name, from Diana
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
I is the Roman numeral one, so a single thing

explanation.surface: A lone woman put in charge of the accounts: what an absurd idea!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping books' suggests bookkeeping, but books is the Old Testament, held between the woman and the in-charge abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something silly enough to deserve mockery is foolish or absurd, which is what both words convey.

clue.text: A nice role working in an Ulster town

indicators.note: working suggests being put into operation and reshaped, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor lands a pleasant job in a Northern Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is used loosely for Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleraine is a real town in County Londonderry, Northern Ireland, on the River Bann near the north coast.

clue.text: Slip made when urchin loses head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its opening letter

parts.note: a naughty, mischievous child is often called a little horror or this

explanation.surface: A street urchin falls and loses their head in the process.
explanation.walkthrough: A little terror is an unruly child; drop the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake or blunder, as in a slip of the tongue, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Young creature associated with a Caribbean island

parts.note: a cub is the young of a bear, lion or fox
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young animal linked to a Caribbean island, like a nature documentary.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the largest island nation in the Caribbean Sea, lying just south of Florida.

clue.text: Panic leads to chap making chewy biscuit

parts.note: a flap is a state of agitated panic, as in getting in a flap
Jack is a common man's name, so any chap

explanation.surface: A man panics while baking a batch of chewy biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a flapjack is a chewy oat bar made with butter and golden syrup, not a pancake as in America.
explanation.definitionFit: British flapjack is a baked oat and syrup traybake cut into bars, eaten like a soft cookie.

clue.text: Fish no guest relished at first unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters end up in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of relished

explanation.surface: Sadly, a fish dish was served that none of the guests enjoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large primitive species of bony fish, famous as the source of caviar.

clue.text: Descending cascade, a force in the north

definitions.meaning: first meaning: water plunging down over a drop
second meaning: in northern English dialect, a force is the local word for this feature

explanation.walkthrough: Force, from Old Norse foss, is the name used in the Lake District and Yorkshire Dales for a cascade, as in Aira Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Water tumbling over a cliff is a cascade, and northern English dialect calls the same thing a force.

clue.text: Correspondence for landlords?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: written messages sent by post

definitions.note: plural noun, matched by the plural answer
definitions.meaning: second meaning: people who let property, read whimsically

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: those who let out rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail sent between people consists of written messages, while property owners who rent out rooms are, humorously, those who let.

clue.text: Dangerous reptiles surrounding union leader in plant

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing on all sides, so the reptiles go around the other piece

parts.note: crocs is short for crocodiles

indicators.note: a leader is at the front, so just the opening letter of the trade body word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of union

explanation.surface: Dangerous crocodiles circling a trade union boss lurking in the undergrowth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union leader' suggests a trade union boss, but it only supplies the first letter of union.
explanation.definitionFit: The crocus is a small spring-flowering bulb with cup-shaped purple, yellow or white blooms.

clue.text: Reliable pianist ultimately out of practice

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the musician word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of pianist
a skill not used for a while gets rusty

explanation.surface: A dependable pianist who has, in the end, let their practice slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dependable can be trusted, and the slightly old-fashioned adjective means faithful or dependable.

clue.text: Calm down about stress

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
strain is pressure or tension, a synonym of stress

explanation.surface: Advice to settle down rather than worry about stress.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back or keep someone under control is to check their agitation, settling them.

clue.text: Senior police officer, first-class

definitions.meaning: first meaning: informal short form for a police superintendent

explanation.walkthrough: In British police forces a superintendent ranks above a chief inspector and is commonly shortened to this.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for a superintendent and also an informal adjective meaning excellent or splendid.

clue.text: Commotion in prison

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fuss or disturbance
second meaning: old slang for jail

explanation.surface: A disturbance breaks out inside a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an excited fuss or disturbance, and in British slang it also means jail.

clue.text: Work on a large gemstone

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical or artistic work
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A jeweller working on a big precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is an iridescent mineral prized as a precious stone in jewellery, often from Australia.

clue.text: Manage to capture small wood

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: to cope is to manage or get by
S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Instructions for successfully seizing a modest patch of woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small wood' looks like the whole definition, but small supplies S and wood alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small group of trees, a little thicket or patch of woodland.

clue.text: Half of them agitate to be ruler

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word means two letters are dropped and two kept

parts.note: taken as written, before halving
to press or agitate is to campaign for something

explanation.surface: Some campaigners stir things up hoping to take power.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the back half of THEM, EM, then add PRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress is a female sovereign governing an empire, so she is a monarch or ruler.

clue.text: Reduce size of quiet skating area

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
a rink is an ice skating surface

explanation.surface: Plans to make a peaceful ice rink smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink something is to make it smaller or contract it, the verb sense matching the clue.

clue.text: Stylish girl in outskirts of Coventry

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the first and last letters of the city name are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Coventry
lass is a northern British word for a girl

explanation.surface: A fashionable girl living on the edge of the city of Coventry.
explanation.walkthrough: C and Y surround LASS: C(LASS)Y. Coventry is a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Classy describes someone elegant and sophisticated in appearance, showing good taste and quality.
